scenes.tts: A rule earns trust when it predicts experiments. How would you test the two signal gate?
scenes.caption: A rule earns trust when it predicts experiments. How would you test the two-signal gate?
scenes.visual: The two-signal formula box from the last chapter, with a lab bench fading in behind it.
scenes.narration: A rule earns trust when it predicts experiments. How would you test the two-signal gate?

scenes.tts: Work in a slice of rat hippocampus. Stimulate the Schaffer collaterals, and record from C A one.
scenes.caption: Work in a slice of rat hippocampus. Stimulate the Schaffer collaterals, and record from CA1.
scenes.visual: A hippocampal slice in a dish; a stimulating electrode on the Schaffer collaterals and a recording electrode in CA1.
scenes.narration: Work in a slice of rat hippocampus. Stimulate the Schaffer collaterals, and record from CA1.

scenes.tts: Give the input its usual fast train, 100 pulses per second. But hold one C A one cell very negative, near minus 90 millivolts.
scenes.caption: Give the input its usual fast train, 100 pulses per second. But hold one CA1 cell very negative, near −90 mV.
scenes.visual: A current electrode in one CA1 cell; its voltage meter is pinned at −90 mV while the 100 Hz train arrives.
scenes.narration: Give the input its usual fast train, 100 pulses per second. But hold one CA1 cell very negative, near −90 mV.

scenes.visual: A question mark over the held cell's time-course plot.

scenes.tts: No, if the current keeps the active spines negative. Then the magnesium block stays strong, and glutamate arrives without the second signal.
scenes.visual: Two meters: the soma at −90 mV and an active spine, also strongly negative, with the note: assume effective hyperpolarization at the active spines. Mg2+ stays lodged in the pore as glutamate binds. The time-course plot stays flat.
scenes.narration: No, if the current keeps the active spines negative. Then the magnesium block stays strong, and glutamate arrives without the second signal.

scenes.tts: In 1986, Malinow and Miller found that hyperpolarizing the cell during the train prevented L T P, under their conditions.
scenes.caption: In 1986, Malinow and Miller found that hyperpolarizing the cell during the train prevented LTP, under their conditions.
scenes.narration: In 1986, Malinow and Miller found that hyperpolarizing the cell during the train prevented LTP, under their conditions.

scenes.tts: The reverse also works. Slow input, too weak to potentiate by itself, was paired with current that depolarized the cell.
scenes.visual: Sparse stimulus ticks, each paired with a depolarizing current step into the cell.
scenes.narration: The reverse also works. Slow input, too weak to potentiate by itself, was paired with current that depolarized the cell.

scenes.tts: That pairing produced L T P. Two groups reported it in 1986.
scenes.caption: That pairing produced LTP. Two groups reported it in 1986.
scenes.visual: The time-course plot rises and stays up. Caption card: Kelso, Ganong and Brown, 1986; Wigström and colleagues, 1986.
scenes.narration: That pairing produced LTP. Two groups reported it in 1986.

scenes.tts: So which matters: how fast the input fires, or whether the cell is depolarized when it does?
scenes.visual: Two cards side by side: frequency, and coincidence.
scenes.narration: So which matters: how fast the input fires, or whether the cell is depolarized when it does?

scenes.tts: Coincidence. High frequency is not required. A fast train is one way to make the cell supply its own depolarization.
scenes.visual: The coincidence card lights up; the frequency card stays, relabelled one way to depolarize.
scenes.narration: Coincidence. High frequency is not required. A fast train is one way to make the cell supply its own depolarization.

scenes.tts: Three experiments tested the gate directly. You have just seen one.
scenes.visual: A checklist: block the receptor; block the calcium; withhold the depolarization (already ticked).
scenes.narration: Three experiments tested the gate directly. You have just seen one.

scenes.tts: First, block the receptor. In 1983, Collingridge, Kehl and McLennan applied the N M D A antagonist A P V.
scenes.caption: First, block the receptor. In 1983, Collingridge, Kehl and McLennan applied the NMDA antagonist APV.
scenes.visual: APV washes into the dish. Caption card: Collingridge, Kehl and McLennan, 1983.
scenes.narration: First, block the receptor. In 1983, Collingridge, Kehl and McLennan applied the NMDA antagonist APV.

scenes.tts: They used doses that abolished responses to an N M D A agonist. The baseline E P S P was unaffected.
scenes.caption: They used doses that abolished responses to an NMDA agonist. The baseline EPSP was unaffected.
scenes.visual: The baseline field EPSP trace is unchanged after APV.
scenes.narration: They used doses that abolished responses to an NMDA agonist. The baseline EPSP was unaffected.

scenes.tts: But a fast train no longer produced L T P. N M D A receptors were needed to start the change, not to carry the everyday response.
scenes.caption: But a fast train no longer produced LTP. NMDA receptors were needed to start the change, not to carry the everyday response.
scenes.visual: A tetanus is given; the time-course plot stays flat. Labels: induction needs NMDA receptors; everyday response does not.
scenes.narration: But a fast train no longer produced LTP. NMDA receptors were needed to start the change, not to carry the everyday response.

scenes.tts: Second, block the calcium. The same year, Lynch and colleagues injected the calcium buffer E G T A into C A one cells.
scenes.caption: Second, block the calcium. The same year, Lynch and colleagues injected the calcium buffer EGTA into CA1 cells.
scenes.visual: A pipette fills one CA1 cell with a buffer that soaks up Ca2+. Caption card: Lynch and colleagues, 1983.
scenes.narration: Second, block the calcium. The same year, Lynch and colleagues injected the calcium buffer EGTA into CA1 cells.

scenes.tts: L T P failed at those cells. So induction needs a calcium rise inside the postsynaptic cell.
scenes.caption: LTP failed at those cells. So induction needs a calcium rise inside the postsynaptic cell.
scenes.visual: The filled cell's plot stays flat while a neighbouring cell potentiates.
scenes.narration: LTP failed at those cells. So induction needs a calcium rise inside the postsynaptic cell.

scenes.tts: With the A P V result, that points to calcium entering through N M D A receptors in active spines.
scenes.caption: With the APV result, that points to calcium entering through NMDA receptors in active spines.
scenes.visual: A bright Ca2+ flash fills the spine. Label: model illustration.
scenes.narration: With the APV result, that points to calcium entering through NMDA receptors in active spines.

scenes.tts: One caution about scope. Not every L T P uses this gate. Mossy fibre L T P, in guinea pig C A three, needed no N M D A receptors.
scenes.caption: One caution about scope. Not every LTP uses this gate. Mossy-fibre LTP, in guinea-pig CA3, needed no NMDA receptors.
scenes.visual: The hippocampus map returns; the mossy fibre to CA3 synapse is marked as the exception.
scenes.narration: One caution about scope. Not every LTP uses this gate. Mossy-fibre LTP, in guinea-pig CA3, needed no NMDA receptors.

scenes.tts: The takeaway: block the N M D A receptor, the calcium, or the depolarization, and L T P fails. Pair glutamate with enough depolarization, and it appears.
scenes.caption: The takeaway: block the NMDA receptor, the calcium, or the depolarization, and LTP fails. Pair glutamate with enough depolarization, and it appears.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card with the three blocks crossed out and the pairing ticked.
scenes.narration: The takeaway: block the NMDA receptor, the calcium, or the depolarization, and LTP fails. Pair glutamate with enough depolarization, and it appears.
